newsitem.title: JAPAN: Omron sees lower 6-mth current profit.
newsitem.headline: Omron sees lower 6-mth current profit.

text.p: Omron Corp said on Thursday that its parent current profit in the six months to September 30, 1996, would be seven billion yen, lower than its original forecast of 7.5 billion yen.
But a spokesman for the maker of electronic control components said that on a full-year basis it would be able to achieve its original target of a parent current profit of 19 billion yen.
The revision of the half-year parent current profit was due to poorer-than-expected performance of its semiconductor-related business, the spokesman said.
He said the company's interim parent sales would be one to two percent lower than its original forecast of 193 billion yen.
In first half of 1995/96, Omron posted a parent current profit of 7.52 billion yen on sales of 190.39 billion yen.
For the full 1996/97, Omron will also be able to achieve its original sales target of 427 billion yen, the spokesman said.
"We think we can achieve our (full-year earnings) forecast as we will be able to complete inventory adjustments and also we will be able to cut production costs," the spokesman said.
Omron plans to announce its half-year earnings on November 20.
